reasons: Overlaps on machine learning, causal inference, computational social science
subject: Interested in your work on heterogeneous treatment effects
body:
Hello Professor Athey,

My name is Vinil Polepalli and I am an undergraduate at New York University studying Computer Science and Business. I have been a research intern in the Chiosis Lab at Memorial Sloan Kettering, where I built protein-ligand graph neural networks for Hsp90 and epichaperome complexes that reached 0.984 ROC AUC separating active from inactive inhibitor candidates.

I read the recursive partitioning paper, and honest estimation is the part that has changed how I look at my own analysis. Using the same observations to choose the partition and to estimate the effect inside it produces intervals confident about structure the data was mined for. My TCGA feature importances were chosen and evaluated on the same 801 samples and presented as findings. I would want to redo that with an honest split.

I would like to hear more about what the group is working on now, and where my background would be useful to you.

In the past, I have worked on the following related projects:
- Sole author, cVAE-augmented deep learning for pan-cancer RNA-seq classification, about 98% test accuracy across 5 cancer types on TCGA: https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.02743
- Hsp90 inhibitor virtual screening in the Chiosis Lab at Memorial Sloan Kettering: 4,566 candidates screened at 0.984 GNN ROC AUC and 5x enrichment, 0 Lipinski violations in the top 50: https://hsp90-dashboard.vercel.app/
- First author, EGCG and piperine synergy in D. tigrina regeneration, IEEE MIT Undergraduate Research Technology Conference: https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/11533121
- Semantic segmentation for UAV-based environmental monitoring at Carnegie Mellon Robotics Institute: 0.88 mean IoU and 0.94 F1 on 25,000 labeled aerial images, sub-100 ms inference across 30 flights

Outside of research I was invited to Y Combinator's Startup School, reached the VEX Robotics World Championship semifinals, and have qualified for the AIME three times.

I have extensively used PyTorch, scikit-learn and Python in past work, along with standard statistical tooling, but have a lot of coding experience and am adaptable to whichever libraries your group uses. My resume is attached. Please let me know if there is a fit in your group.

I would be happy to elaborate on my skills and where I think I can best help out.

Thank you!

--
Vinil Polepalli
New York University | Class of 2029
B.S. Computer Science and B.S. Business
